subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin is a dwarf raised by hill giants, struggling to reconcile his dual heritage and seeking acceptance into a dwarven clan. He is emotionally grounded by his bond with Dawnbringer and has formed deep, unspoken alliances with his companions after surviving the Underdark.
source_quote: I'm a dwarf. I'm not invited along.

subject: Eldeth
fact: Eldeth is a dwarven noble bound by duty to report the dangers of the Underdark to Mithral Hall and Gauntlgrym. She recognizes Thorin’s worth beyond clan norms and has sworn to formally embrace him into her clan after delivering her briefing.
source_quote: I swear.

subject: Dawnbringer
fact: Dawnbringer is a sentient magical sword with agency, warmth, and a personality shaped by months of darkness and now the open sky. She shares a profound, non-verbal bond with Thorin and is unapologetically self-aware, even when called annoying.
source_quote: I'm annoying also, Dawnbringer. Look, you know, we got each other.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir is a former Ember Vanguard monk trained in reading environmental stillness and threat vectors. He remains hyper-vigilant after months underground and has developed a quiet, wordless rapport with his companions, especially in moments of danger.
source_quote: The deer.

subject: Glabbagool
fact: Glabbagool is an ooze with unexpected sentience and capacity for witness. Despite lacking fixed appendages or conventional mobility, he demonstrates focused stillness and awareness, prompting Zalthir to consider him as a potential monk candidate.
source_quote: Glabbagool just looked up.

subject: Spiderbait
fact: Spiderbait is a goblin who has never been to the surface and is navigating social integration with cautious optimism. He seeks safety through proximity to larger, more accepted companions rather than direct confrontation with prejudice.
source_quote: Do you mind if I just sort of hang out with you guys?

subject: Daz
fact: Daz is a methodical, observant companion who relies on precision and analysis. He shares Zalthir’s awareness of environmental anomalies and contributes to the group’s silent consensus on threats.
source_quote: Daz squinted and pushed his spectacles up and looked like a man calculating the precise angle of the light source.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum is a pragmatic, dice-rolling companion whose confidence often masks deep intuition. He is protective of small or vulnerable beings and serves as the group’s emotional anchor in moments of tension.
source_quote: You conclude, that what is following you is a deer.

subject: Clan of Mithral Hall
fact: The dwarven clan of Mithral Hall holds authority over surface knowledge of the Underdark and is the intended recipient of Eldeth’s report. They are perceived as gatekeepers of tradition, but Eldeth believes they will extend inclusion to Thorin once the truth is presented.
source_quote: I am certain they will want to speak to you, and I will make it a statement of purpose that you shall be embraced by our clan.

subject: Ember Vanguard
fact: The Ember Vanguard is a monastic order with specialized training in environmental threat detection and silent communication. Zalthir’s training within this order enables the group to recognize covert surveillance without verbal confirmation.
source_quote: The three of you quickly realize... that somebody's following you.

subject: departure from Candlekeep's tunnel
fact: The group emerges from the Underdark into sunlight at Candlekeep’s tunnel mouth, marking the end of their subterranean journey and the beginning of their transition to the surface world. Each member reacts differently, reflecting their trauma, hope, and adaptation.
source_quote: The sun. I keep coming back to that first moment of it...

subject: Eldeth’s oath to Thorin
fact: Eldeth formally swears to secure Thorin’s acceptance into her clan after delivering her report to the dwarven lords, transforming what could have been a farewell into a promise of belonging.
source_quote: I swear.

subject: detection of hidden pursuer
fact: On the third day of surface travel, Zalthir and his companions detect a silent, patient follower in the northern treeline — an entity that mimics natural stillness and has been tracking them since emerging from the Underdark.
source_quote: The trees north of us were wrong.

subject: Candlekeep
fact: Candlekeep is a landmark on the surface, situated west of the Underdark exit, serving as a neutral ground and potential sanctuary. It is referenced as a destination for both Eldeth’s journey and Spiderbait’s hope for safety.
source_quote: Head west and you'll hit Candlekeep.

subject: Mithral Hall
fact: Mithral Hall is a dwarven stronghold and political center where Eldeth must deliver her report on the Underdark’s dangers. It represents the threshold between the hidden world and surface authority, and the potential gateway to Thorin’s acceptance.
source_quote: I must go to Mithral Hall.

subject: Dawnbringer
fact: Dawnbringer is a sentient, warm-hilted magical sword that radiates emotional resonance. It is not merely a weapon but a companion with personality, history, and agency — capable of affection, sarcasm, and silent understanding.
source_quote: I'm annoying also, Dawnbringer.

subject: Hidden pursuer
fact: An unidentified entity is following the group with expert patience, using terrain and timing to remain undetected. It moves with intention, avoiding detection even from trained observers, and is not a deer despite Grygum’s roll.
source_quote: Oh, no. It's not a deer.

subject: Thorin’s dwarven identity
fact: Thorin’s journey to reconcile his giant upbringing with his dwarven heritage remains unresolved. Eldeth’s oath offers a path, but whether the clan will accept him — and how he will define himself — is an open thread.
source_quote: I do want to learn about my dwarven roots.

subject: the pursuer’s identity
fact: The identity, motive, and origin of the hidden follower remain unknown. Its presence suggests deeper, surface-level threats connected to Underdark events — a looming danger not yet named.
source_quote: Whatever was in those trees had been moving with us... Patient.

subject: Glabbagool’s monk potential
fact: Zalthir’s contemplation of Glabbagool as a monk candidate introduces an unprecedented question: can an ooze embody discipline, stillness, and spiritual growth? This thread challenges traditional definitions of monasticism.
source_quote: He's got the stillness working for him.

subject: third day of open sky
fact: The events of the hidden pursuer’s detection occur on the third day after emerging from the Underdark, marking a psychological transition point where surface normalcy begins to fray under lingering trauma.
source_quote: The third day of open sky and I still hadn't stopped scanning.

subject: dusk
fact: The pursuer is detected at dusk — a time of diminished visibility and heightened vulnerability — which the entity appears to have chosen deliberately or stumbled into through patience.
source_quote: Dusk came in from the west...

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir is a disciplined and efficient combatant who neutralizes threats with surgical precision, as demonstrated when he grappled and stunned the drow spy without hesitation, establishing immediate control over the situation.
source_quote: Zalthir had already ended the question of whether there would be a fight. There would not. The spy — drow, slight, female, exactly as advertised — was grappled and stunned, held in place with the kind of efficient finality that Zalthir brings to everything he considers a problem worth solving immediately.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin is a battle-hardened dwarf whose physical presence and blunt tactics often intimidate but rarely manipulate drow; his attempts at psychological pressure are ineffective yet reveal his unwavering honesty and lack of political subtlety.
source_quote: He walked up and told her we could simply let her go — report her failure to her matron, 'let them know how pathetic you are.' He said this with the confidence of someone who thought he was offering a fate worse than death.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum possesses an intuitive, almost mystical perception that cuts through social armor; his unexpected offer of employment and non-threatening presentation of prayer beads disarmed the drow spy more effectively than threats or violence.
source_quote: Hey, are you looking for a new job? We could use another helper." and "He didn't say anything particularly ominous. He just handed them to her and told her to put them on. No threat in his voice. No explanation of what they did.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz is a highly observant and psychologically astute drow who reads subtle behavioral cues — especially in drow social dynamics — and uses calm, precise interrogation to extract truth, often bypassing conventional methods through insight rather than force.
source_quote: She wasn't watching the party. She was watching me. And working very, very hard to make it look like she wasn't." and "So basically, you're treating me as bait. You're watching and observing so that when something happens to me, you can go report back what happened to me.

subject: Glabbagool
fact: Glabbagool is a creature with no conceptual framework for natural phenomena like birdsong, yet he attempts to emulate them with enthusiastic, unrecognizable results — his lack of understanding is so profound it becomes a form of unintentional comedy and philosophical disruption.
source_quote: His impression of a bird was everything you'd expect from a creature that has never encountered a bird, never encountered the concept of sound being produced intentionally for communication purposes, and was working from approximately zero reference points.

subject: House T'sarran
fact: House T'sarran is an ancient, stable drow house with two centuries of unchallenged rule; it operates with patience and long-term strategy, assigning agents to observe rather than attack, indicating a focus on intelligence gathering over immediate dominance.
source_quote: My matron has ruled House T'sarran for two hundred years." and "The matron mother was interested in you... We are looking for the one who paid to have you protected.

subject: Drow Spy
fact: The drow spy is a young, overburdened operative assigned to an unfamiliar and hostile surface environment; her training prevents open aggression, but her psychological resilience breaks under non-threatening, alien stimuli — revealing her as a reluctant agent rather than a committed enemy.
source_quote: I was just assigned to track you, not to engage." and "She stared at him blankly. The stun was still doing its work; I'm not sure she'd fully processed the comment.

subject: Surface Forest Near the Road
fact: The surface forest is a disorienting, overbright environment for drow, where natural sounds and daylight act as psychological weapons; its openness and unfamiliarity expose the spy's vulnerability and undermine her training.
source_quote: The overbright that was already making her eyes ache." and "Months in the Underdark will calibrate your instincts. You learn to notice the shape of a threat before you can name it.

subject: Prayer Beads
fact: The prayer beads are an artifact of an alien faith, wielded not as a weapon but as an instrument of psychological disruption; their unknown function and presentation by a half-orc cleric shattered the drow spy’s mental defenses more effectively than any threat.
source_quote: Grygum held out the prayer beads... She looked at a half-orc cleric holding out holy symbols of a deity she knew nothing about... That slipped right past every prepared defense.

subject: The Patron Who Paid for Daz's Protection
fact: An unknown patron paid to protect Daz, triggering House T'sarran’s long-term surveillance operation; this revelation suggests a hidden political or magical debt that predates Daz’s return to the surface and may involve powerful forces beyond the Underdark.
source_quote: We are looking for the one who paid to have you protected.

subject: Surface Encounter Timeline
fact: The events occurred during daylight hours on the surface, following months of underground travel and recent emergence from Blingdenstone; the timing is critical as it marks the first time Daz has been exposed to open daylight since leaving Menzoberranzan.
source_quote: I've been away from home for a while." and "conducting interrogations in full sunlight while running on whatever sleep we'd managed in Blingdenstone.

subject: Drow Spy Interrogation
fact: The interrogation succeeded not through force or fear, but through psychological misdirection, non-threatening offers, and the introduction of the unknown — Grygum’s employment proposal and the prayer beads triggered the spy’s collapse, revealing critical intelligence about House T'sarran’s motives.
source_quote: She talked." and "The beads were the thing that actually broke through the professional armor.

subject: Daz's Identity as a Target
fact: Daz is not merely being followed — he is being used as bait to draw out the patron who protected him; this implies he carries a hidden significance or debt that even his own people in House T'sarran do not fully understand, suggesting a deeper, possibly divine or arcane, origin to his past.
source_quote: My matron believes that the one who paid — for him — will reveal themselves once he reaches the surface.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz is a drow who has lived away from Menzoberranzan long enough to lose his social fluency in the city, yet retains the deep, instinctual reading of drow behavior — making him uniquely vulnerable and uniquely perceptive in this encounter.
source_quote: You realize how absurd that sounds?" and "I'm drow, but I've been underground for a while.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz is an eighth-level wizard who kept four people alive through the Underdark, demon lords, and House politics, and has been valuable because someone with resources believes observing what happens to him may reveal a person they are interested in.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum possesses prayer beads at full power despite being shrunken, believes they may be more deadly, and holds a Revivify spell; he is the one who proposed and orchestrated the plan to temporarily kill Daz to test who is protecting him.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin is skeptical of all deception, insists on practical solutions, and ordered the miniaturization of the drow spy into a 'Polly Pocket' size, then mandated her containment in a bag of holding with holes for ventilation and shielding from sunlight as an act of calculated mercy.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir is the Pocket Spy, now miniaturized and contained in the bag of holding, and is the subject of active theoretical murder planning by the party; her fate is tied to the interrogation of who is protecting Daz.

subject: Glabbagool
fact: Glabbagool is an ooze who has spent days in the bag of holding with the miniaturized drow spy as his only company, watches her with one unblinking eye, and is the only member of the party with no social conditioning around knowledge limits — he is confused why the party does not donate all books to Candlekeep to ask unlimited questions.

subject: House T'sarran
fact: House T'sarran sent the miniaturized drow spy to gather intelligence on Daz and the party, and has demonstrated the capacity to send additional agents even if the current spy is captured or killed.

subject: Candlekeep
fact: Candlekeep requires one book per group for entry, but grants increased 'FaceTime' with avowed sages for each additional book provided; the party submitted five books — including the Velkynvelve Prisoner Journal, Ilvara's prayer book with Zuggtmoy marginalia, and Asha Vandree's theological treatise — to gain access and ask multiple questions.

subject: prayer beads
fact: The prayer beads are shrunken but operating at full power, possibly more deadly than their original form, and are being used by Grygum as a tool of psychological pressure against the drow spy.

subject: bag of holding
fact: The bag of holding contains the miniaturized drow spy, is ventilated with holes for breathing, is shielded from sunlight as a mercy, and is carried by Glabbagool, who watches her with one eye while walking.

subject: Velkynvelve Prisoner Journal
fact: The Velkynvelve Prisoner Journal is one of five books submitted to Candlekeep; it was received with reverence by the First Reader and is considered a masterpiece of drow prison documentation.

subject: temporary death of Daz
fact: Grygum proposed and the party agreed to temporarily kill Daz using a Revivify spell to determine who is protecting him; the plan was treated as a controlled experiment with no enforcement mechanism beyond mutual interest.

subject: miniaturization of the drow spy
fact: The drow spy was shrunk to the size of a child's toy using a mushroom, rendered voice-pitched and indignant, and given the demeaning nickname 'Polly Pocket' by Thorin; she is now contained in the bag of holding under Glabbagool’s surveillance.

subject: submission of five books to Candlekeep
fact: The party submitted five books — Princess Ebonmire’s spellbook, Ilvara’s prayer book, Asha Vandree’s theological argument, the Velkynvelve Prisoner Journal, and Pliinki’s journal — to gain FaceTime with Candlekeep’s avowed; this exceeded the standard one-book requirement and enabled multiple questions to be asked.

subject: Glabbagool's question at Candlekeep
fact: Glabbagool, the ooze, was granted one question at Candlekeep despite having no prior social conditioning around knowledge limits; his confusion over why the party does not donate all books to ask unlimited questions was noted as a bracing perspective.

subject: who is protecting Daz
fact: The entire party’s strategy revolves around determining who is protecting Daz — whether through magical surveillance, divine intervention, or hidden allegiance — and the temporary death plan, the prayer beads, and the spy’s containment are all tools to expose that protector.

subject: Glabbagool's one question
fact: Glabbagool’s single question at Candlekeep remains unknown, but the party is intensely curious what a creature with no past, no allegiances, and a singular earnest interest in understanding the world would choose to know — and the answer may redefine their understanding of knowledge itself.

subject: Candlekeep
fact: Candlekeep is an enormous, self-important library with rules requiring one book per group for entry and granting increased access to sages for additional books; it houses vast archives of drow prison journals and is the destination for the party’s mission to interrogate hidden truths.

subject: bag of holding interior
fact: The interior of the bag of holding is a confined, dark space where the miniaturized drow spy is held with holes for ventilation and shielded from sunlight; Glabbagool watches her with one eye, making it the most surveilled and psychologically oppressive prison the party has devised.

subject: journey to Candlekeep
fact: The journey to Candlekeep lasted weeks, during which the party developed their plan to use the drow spy as bait, miniaturized her, contained her, and prepared their five books for entry — a period of psychological manipulation, logistical planning, and philosophical reflection.

subject: Glabbagool
fact: Glabbagool is an ooze capable of producing proliferating eyes as affectations to appear friendly, but his true perception is non-human; he has been assigned the task of watching the miniaturized drow spy continuously in the bag of holding, and his steady, unblinking attention is the most earnest form of control the party has.

subject: the drow spy
fact: The drow spy, now miniaturized and known as 'Polly Pocket,' is a captured agent of House T'sarran who was shrunk, contained, surveilled, and subjected to misinformation about prayer beads and the threat of death; she is being used as bait to expose who is protecting Daz, and is visibly reconsidering her options.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum is cited by Daz at every available opportunity, making Malfire references an ambient weather condition within the party, and has been pulled into discussions about this habit.
source_quote: We had been through enough together that the citations had become a kind of ambient weather condition, something you adapted to rather than fought.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin responded immediately and mercilessly to demands for information, refusing questions and asserting that no book was donated, and later received directional instruction regarding Philemon with the quiet satisfaction of someone who had hoped for exactly those words.
source_quote: You don't get a question. You did not donate a book.", "Thorin received this information like a man who has been hoping someone would say exactly these words.

subject: Vareth
fact: Vareth is a half-elf scholar with a decades-long specialty in half-orc Bahamut converts, a previously obscure niche that became a flood after a living half-orc cleric of Bahamut entered his life, and he now has funding, conference invitations, and a newly coined term — 'Stroud's Gambit' — to anchor his research.
source_quote: He grabbed my hand and practically dragged me.", "The field of Bahamut half-orc conversions will benefit tremendously from your interview.

subject: Stroud
fact: Stroud, a dwarf who cannot actually play chess, defeated Protanther — an ancient gold dragon who had analyzed the same position for four hundred years — by rolling a move that landed perfectly and definitively, triggering Protanther’s defection to the alliance and reshaping scholarly understanding of divine intervention.
source_quote: Stroud rolled — and it landed perfectly. Definitively. The kind of thing that doesn't just work, it announces itself.

subject: Protanther
fact: Protanther is an ancient gold dragon who spent four hundred years mapping every possible chess move in a single position, was certain of the outcome, and was so stunned by Stroud’s unexpected victory that he joined the alliance.
source_quote: Protanther had mapped every possible move. He was certain. And then Stroud rolled — and it landed perfectly.

subject: Philemon
fact: Philemon is an avowed monk specializing in psychological preservation and historical cataloging of ancient sentient artifacts, with a tremendous track record of success in resolving interpersonal conflict among sentient artifacts, and was the subject of directional instruction given to Thorin and Dawnbringer.
source_quote: an avowed monk specializing in psychological preservation and historical cataloging of ancient sentient artifacts, with a tremendous track record of success in working through the interpersonal conflict issues of the sentient artifact.

subject: Dawnbringer
fact: Dawnbringer received directional instruction regarding Philemon alongside Thorin, and was the subject of a personal remark from the speaker about needing couples counseling, which was acknowledged as correct.
source_quote: I'm all up for couples counseling with Dawnbringer.", "Good. They needed it.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir was assigned by the First Reader to investigate the Jimjar thread, which dovetailed neatly with an avowed named Khell-Vire who wanted to learn about something specific — and not about the party generally, but about the speaker in particular.
source_quote: Zalthir got the Jimjar thread — which apparently dovetailed neatly with an avowed named Khell-Vire who wanted to learn about something specific. The First Reader clarified: not about the party generally, but about me in particular.

subject: The First Reader
fact: The First Reader assigned scholars to investigate threads related to the speaker, clarified that inquiries were about the speaker personally and not the party, and was the target of Vareth’s outrage over withheld information regarding a cleric of Bahamut.
source_quote: The First Reader assigned scholars.", "I cannot believe you did not tell me about the arrival of a cleric of Bahamut.

subject: Bahamut's followers
fact: Bahamut’s followers have experienced a surge of scholarly and theological interest due to the emergence of a half-orc cleric, sparking debates about whether this signals a divine plan, and triggering a reevaluation of the orc pantheon’s relationship with draconic deities.
source_quote: What did the sudden half-orc interest in Bahamut mean for the orc pantheon? Was it part of Bahamut's plan?

subject: Stroud's Gambit
fact: Stroud's Gambit is the newly coined term describing the improbable, perfectly timed chess move by Stroud that defeated Protanther after four centuries of analysis, and has become a foundational concept in Vareth’s research on divine intervention and accidental revelation.
source_quote: Stroud's Gambit.", "The field of Bahamut half-orc conversions will benefit tremendously from your interview.

subject: arrival of a half-orc cleric of Bahamut
fact: The arrival of a living half-orc cleric of Bahamut into Vareth’s study transformed his decades-long obscure research into a flood of funding, conference invitations, and scholarly controversy, marking a paradigm shift in draconic theology.
source_quote: A living half-orc cleric of Bahamut had walked through his door.

subject: theological implications of half-orc Bahamut conversions
fact: The theological implications of half-orc conversions to Bahamut remain unresolved, with scholars debating whether this reflects divine strategy, cultural evolution, or accidental alignment, and the speaker’s personal experience is now a central data point.
source_quote: What did the sudden half-orc interest in Bahamut mean for the orc pantheon? Was it part of Bahamut's plan?

subject: Candlekeep
fact: Candlekeep is the location where scholars are assigned threads, where Vareth confronts the First Reader, where Stroud defeats Protanther, and where the speaker gathers notes on theological documents, prayer books, and Underdark evidence.
source_quote: Somewhere in the library, there were answers waiting. About Bahamut's intentions, about what my conversion meant in the broader theological landscape...

subject: prayer book
fact: The prayer book is one of the speaker’s accumulated notes and pieces of evidence gathered during months in the Underdark, now being used to interrogate theological questions in Candlekeep.
source_quote: I had notes — the prayer book, the theological documents, the accumulated evidence of months in the Underdark...

subject: theological documents
fact: Theological documents are among the speaker’s accumulated notes from months in the Underdark, now being referenced to understand Bahamut’s intentions and the significance of the speaker’s conversion.
source_quote: I had notes — the prayer book, the theological documents, the accumulated evidence of months in the Underdark...

subject: Protanther
fact: Protanther is an ancient gold dragon who spent four hundred years analyzing a single chess position, was certain of all outcomes, and was defeated by Stroud’s unexpected move — a rare instance of a monster being emotionally and ideologically transformed by an opponent’s ignorance.
source_quote: Protanther had mapped every possible move. He was certain. And then Stroud rolled — and it landed perfectly.

subject: four hundred years
fact: Four hundred years is the duration Protanther spent analyzing the same chess position, establishing a temporal anchor for the event of Stroud’s Gambit and highlighting the scale of preparation that still contained a blind spot.
source_quote: an ancient gold dragon who had been analyzing the same position for four hundred years.

subject: Malfire citations
fact: The persistent citation of Malfire by Daz has become an ambient, unspoken norm within the party, so ingrained that it is referenced as a condition of their relationship, and the speaker confirms its accuracy by invoking Volume 3.
source_quote: It's like we're kind of sick of each other, but somehow still together, yeah.", "As Malfire said in Volume 3.

subject: The Speaker
fact: The speaker is a half-orc cleric of Bahamut whose personal conversion has become the central data point in Vareth’s research, is the subject of scholarly inquiry regarding divine intent, and has coined the term 'Stroud's Gambit' to describe a paradigm-shifting event that redefined academic understanding of accidental revelation.
source_quote: I haven't moved into that phase yet.", "Stroud's Gambit.", "I took notes. It's what I do.
